steps.title: Recruit and mobilise the core multidisciplinary digital product team
steps.summary: Recruit, appoint or assign the four-person first-year core from September through November 2026: two full-stack engineers, one product and experience designer and one agile delivery manager. Confirm named specialist support from wider Digital and IT for architecture, integration, quality, research and assurance where needed.

outputs.title: Four-person core team
outputs.summary: Recruit or assign two full-stack engineers, one product and experience designer and one agile delivery manager, including hands-on technical leadership within the engineering capacity.

outputs.title: Named specialist support
outputs.summary: Confirm how architecture, data, integration, quality, security, accessibility, service design, user research and service management will be drawn in when the work genuinely requires them.

outputs.title: Leadership and decision rights
outputs.summary: Confirm who leads the team, how product and technical decisions are made and how capacity conflicts are escalated.

outputs.title: Initial pipeline and capacity plan
outputs.summary: Create one prioritised view of the King’s Edge roadmap, thin Hub work, available capacity and known constraints.

existingCapacity.owner: Digital and IT with King’s Edge sponsorship
existingCapacity.contribution: Provide product leadership, institutional prioritisation and resolution of competing demand.
existingCapacity.riskIfMissing: The team may receive conflicting demand or lack authority to protect agreed delivery commitments.

existingCapacity.role: Specialist architecture, integration, quality and assurance support
existingCapacity.contribution: Provide named specialist contributors when the first-year scope requires them, without assuming all specialist capability must be permanently funded inside the core pod.
existingCapacity.riskIfMissing: The core team may be blocked by specialist queues or lack expertise at key decisions.

existingCapacity.role: Proportionate service design and user research support
existingCapacity.owner: Digital and IT with the Student Experience Hub sponsor
existingCapacity.contribution: Supplement the product and experience designer where the thin Hub or later journey work needs deeper research or service-design input.
existingCapacity.riskIfMissing: The product designer may be stretched if a larger research programme is added without extra capacity.

existingCapacity.contribution: Provide named service-management and support counterparts so delivery and live operation are planned together.
existingCapacity.riskIfMissing: The team may deliver capabilities without a credible route into ongoing support.

newInvestment.estimatedCost: Indicative £201,000 in constant 2026 prices for November 2026 to June 2027.
newInvestment.fundingRoute: TBC through the mobilisation business case
newInvestment.rationale: Two full-stack engineers, one product and experience designer and one agile delivery manager, including hands-on technical leadership within the engineering capacity. This returns the first-year planning assumption to the lean core that preceded the August acceleration. Additional specialist capacity should be assigned from existing teams or costed separately only where confirmed scope and technical discovery demonstrate a genuine gap.
newInvestment.riskIfMissing: The institution will not establish the in-house core required to replatform King’s Edge and create the first Hub foundations.

enablingConditions.condition: Approve the four-person first-year core and recruitment route in time for recruitment to begin in September 2026.
enablingConditions.owner: Digital and IT with King’s Edge sponsorship
enablingConditions.riskIfMissing: The core team will not be available for the planned November mobilisation.

enablingConditions.condition: Assign named specialist contributors with clear routes for timely input rather than embedding additional permanent first-year roles by default.
enablingConditions.riskIfMissing: The lean core may be blocked when specialist decisions are needed.

enablingConditions.condition: Keep the September 2027 Hub proposition thin. Any material increase in integration depth must trigger an explicit review of scope, timing and team capacity.
enablingConditions.owner: King’s Edge Portfolio Board and Digital and IT
enablingConditions.riskIfMissing: The four-person planning assumption may be undermined by unacknowledged scope growth.

steps.title: Establish the product operating model and delivery practices
steps.summary: From November 2026 to February 2027, establish one transparent product pipeline, prioritisation and capacity cadence, proportionate discovery and user involvement, engineering and quality expectations, embedded assurance and release practices across the King’s Edge roadmap and thin Hub work.

outputs.title: Demand intake and prioritisation
outputs.summary: Create one transparent route for new demand, triage, sequencing and capacity decisions.

outputs.title: Capacity and trade-off rules
outputs.summary: Make the King’s Edge commitment, thin Hub work and available capacity visible, and require explicit decisions when new scope would displace agreed work.

outputs.title: Proportionate discovery and user involvement
outputs.summary: Use the level of research, service design and prototyping appropriate to the decision being made rather than applying a fixed heavyweight lifecycle.

outputs.title: Engineering, quality and assurance practices
outputs.summary: Agree practical code review, testing, documentation and embedded assurance expectations appropriate to the team and product risk.

outputs.title: Release discipline
outputs.summary: Define proportionate criteria for controlled release, support readiness and learning from live use.

steps.title: Prove the product capability through King’s Edge and the thin Hub release
steps.summary: From January to October 2027, prove that the core team can deliver the substantive King’s Edge roadmap while also establishing the common Hub shell and light-touch service access for September. Use delivery evidence to identify any real capacity gaps before expanding the team.

outputs.title: Substantive King’s Edge delivery
outputs.summary: Move the replatform and agreed richer Edge capabilities predictably through build, test and controlled release.

outputs.title: Thin Hub delivery
outputs.summary: Deliver the common home and agreed light-touch timetable, KEATS and Ask King’s access without turning these into parallel deep integration programmes.

outputs.title: Continuous student and service involvement
outputs.summary: Use proportionate testing and service-owner input to shape decisions throughout delivery.

outputs.title: Evidence-led capacity review
outputs.summary: Use actual throughput, quality, integration effort and live-service obligations to decide whether the team needs to expand for 2027/28.

newInvestment.item: Possible Year 2 digital product team expansion
newInvestment.estimatedCost: Up to an indicative £407,000 for 2027/28 in constant 2026 prices if the team expands to 5.5 FTE.
newInvestment.fundingRoute: TBC through the mobilisation business case
newInvestment.fundingStatus: Provisional ceiling only; evidence-based decision required
newInvestment.rationale: This is a maximum planning envelope rather than an assumed Year 2 team shape. The May 2027 review should use confirmed wider-Hub roadmap demand, live-service obligations, actual integration effort, delivery throughput and quality evidence to decide whether extra engineering or quality capacity is justified.
newInvestment.riskIfMissing: If evidence demonstrates a real need to expand and no funding route exists, live-service or wider-Hub work may compete with the continuing product roadmap.

enablingConditions.condition: Do not carry the 5.5 FTE shape forward automatically. Re-earn any expansion through the May 2027 capacity review.
enablingConditions.owner: Digital and IT product capability leadership with King’s Edge Portfolio Board
enablingConditions.riskIfMissing: A temporary response to an inflated first-year scope may become a permanent staffing assumption.

steps.title: Make product operations and live-service collaboration routine
steps.summary: From November 2027 to February 2028, make the team’s operating practices routine across the live Student Experience Hub and King’s Edge product domain, balancing roadmap delivery, incidents, maintenance, quality, discovery and continuous improvement.

outputs.title: Routine pipeline and capacity cadence
outputs.summary: Maintain a transparent backlog and regular prioritisation and capacity decisions across product demands.

outputs.title: Predictable discovery and release rhythm
outputs.summary: Establish a repeatable cadence that balances discovery, delivery, quality, release and evaluation.

outputs.title: Live-service feedback loop
outputs.summary: Connect incidents, support evidence, maintenance and service performance directly into product prioritisation.

outputs.title: Ownership and handover model
outputs.summary: Clarify when the team retains responsibility, collaborates with service owners or transfers an enduring capability.

outputs.title: Product evidence and benefits review
outputs.summary: Use product analytics, research and operational evidence to assess value and decide what happens next.

steps.title: Scale the team and its practices where the wider roadmap justifies it
steps.summary: From March to October 2028, expand or reshape the team only where live-service evidence and the confirmed wider student-journey roadmap justify additional throughput or specialist capability.

outputs.title: Evidence-led team shape
outputs.summary: Set roles and capacity against confirmed demand, throughput, quality and service evidence.

outputs.title: Consistent product practices
outputs.summary: Apply common product, research, design, engineering, quality and assurance expectations as the roadmap expands.

outputs.title: Balanced delivery and live-service capacity
outputs.summary: Plan explicitly for new development, maintenance, support, technical improvement and research.

newInvestment.estimatedCost: Up to an indicative £407,000 for 2028/29 in constant 2026 prices if the confirmed roadmap still requires a 5.5 FTE team.
newInvestment.decisionNeededBy: Before the 2028/29 staffing plan is fixed
newInvestment.fundingRoute: TBC through the mobilisation business case
newInvestment.fundingStatus: Provisional ceiling only; evidence-based decision required
newInvestment.rationale: Retains a planning ceiling for the final intensive mobilisation year without assuming that the role mix or full 5.5 FTE will still be required.
newInvestment.riskIfMissing: If confirmed demand exceeds the sustainable core and expansion cannot be funded, delivery or live-service capacity may be constrained.

steps.title: Embed an enduring institutional product-development capability
steps.summary: From November 2028 to June 2029, establish the multidisciplinary team, its recurrent staffing, professional leadership, governance, product practices and interfaces with product owners and specialist Digital and IT services as an enduring institutional capability.

outputs.title: Recurrent team and funding model
outputs.summary: Confirm the sustainable core staffing and funding route beyond mobilisation.

outputs.title: Enduring governance and decision rights
outputs.summary: Confirm authority over the pipeline, capacity, methods and escalation routes.

outputs.title: Professional leadership and career routes
outputs.summary: Embed role development, professional standards, mentoring and progression for the multidisciplinary team.

outputs.title: Stable specialist and service interfaces
outputs.summary: Confirm how the team works with architecture, data, integration, assurance, service management and product owners.

outputs.title: Continuous-improvement operating model
outputs.summary: Maintain regular discovery, delivery, evaluation and practice improvement after mobilisation ends.

newInvestment.estimatedCost: Indicative £263,000 annual recurrent cost in constant 2026 prices.
newInvestment.decisionNeededBy: Before recurrent budgets and organisational structures are fixed for 2029/30
newInvestment.fundingRoute: Recurrent Digital and IT baseline, TBC
newInvestment.rationale: Retains two full-stack engineers, approximately 0.75 FTE product and experience design and approximately 0.75 FTE agile delivery and product operations. This should be reset against evidence before final approval.
newInvestment.riskIfMissing: The institution will lose the multidisciplinary development capability created through mobilisation.

enablingConditions.condition: Reset the recurrent team model against live-service demand and the confirmed long-term Hub roadmap before final approval.
enablingConditions.owner: Digital and IT with institutional investment governance
enablingConditions.riskIfMissing: A historic mobilisation assumption may be carried into business as usual without evidence.

enablingConditions.condition: Confirm enduring product-capability leadership, prioritisation governance and the relationship to the Hub product and platform ownership under 4.1.2.
enablingConditions.owner: Digital and IT with the accountable Student Experience Hub sponsor
enablingConditions.decisionNeededBy: Before transition to business as usual
enablingConditions.riskIfMissing: The permanent team may lack clear authority over its pipeline, practices and capacity.
